nodes.name: Open Remediation Run

parameters.query:
-- Open the run ledger entry. Shared table, source='remediation-executor'.
--
-- The same statement counts the work waiting, so the readiness check costs no
-- extra round trip and is recorded against the run that acted on it.
--
-- WHAT COUNTS AS WORK: rows in salesops.remediation_pending_execution, which
-- contains only actions a human explicitly authorised (status 'approved', or
-- 'failed' with retry budget left) and never one still 'proposed'. This
-- workflow therefore selects nothing. It cannot grade an anomaly, cannot
-- choose an action, and cannot authorise one - it runs what a person already
-- said to run.
--
-- Note what is NOT part of readiness: whether Stage 6, 7 or 8 ran today.
-- Remediation executes an approval a human gave, possibly days ago. Making it
-- wait on an upstream pipeline would mean a failed FX sync could silently
-- block an authorised investigation.
WITH work AS (
    SELECT count(*)                                              AS authorized,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE severity = 'critical')         AS critical,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE status   = 'failed')           AS retrying
    FROM salesops.remediation_pending_execution
),
unauthorized AS (
    SELECT count(*) AS n FROM salesops.remediation_actions WHERE status = 'proposed'
)
INSERT INTO salesops.ingestion_runs
    (batch_id, source, window_from, window_to, status, n8n_execution_id)
SELECT
    gen_random_uuid(),
    'remediation-executor',
    COALESCE((SELECT min(calendar_date) FROM salesops.remediation_pending_execution),
             CURRENT_DATE),
    COALESCE((SELECT max(calendar_date) FROM salesops.remediation_pending_execution),
             CURRENT_DATE),
    'running',
    $1
RETURNING
    batch_id::text    AS batch_id,
    run_id,
    window_from::text AS window_from,
    window_to::text   AS window_to,
    (SELECT authorized FROM work)::int   AS authorized_actions,
    (SELECT critical   FROM work)::int   AS critical_actions,
    (SELECT retrying   FROM work)::int   AS retrying_actions,
    -- Visible, and deliberately NOT actionable here: an action nobody has
    -- authorised is not this workflow's to advance.
    (SELECT n FROM unauthorized)::int    AS awaiting_authorization,
    ((SELECT authorized FROM work) > 0)  AS has_authorized_work;

nodes.notes: Opens ingestion_runs with source='remediation-executor' and counts the authorised work waiting. Reads remediation_pending_execution, which never contains an unauthorised action.

nodes.name: Approved Work Waiting?
nodes.notes: Stage 9 does nothing unless a human authorised something. That is the whole stage, and it is worth being visible in the shape of the workflow rather than only in the service.

nodes.name: Execute Approved Actions
nodes.notes: Service-name DNS, never localhost. NO CREDENTIALS HERE - the recording provider needs none, and a real provider would read its own from the service environment, never from this JSON or its execution history. NO ACTION SELECTION HERE either: the service reads remediation_pending_execution, so this node cannot choose what runs, and no LLM output reaches it in any form. `actor` is 'stage9-workflow' and never a person - the workflow executes; it does not approve. Retry is safe because execution is idempotent: claiming an action is a conditional UPDATE, so a second attempt runs only what did not complete. On failure it routes to the second output rather than throwing, so this workflow always closes its own ledger entry.

nodes.name: Finalize Remediation Run

parameters.query:
-- Close the run, deriving the status from what the service actually did.
--
-- 'failed'  every authorised action failed to execute. Nothing about the
--           approvals changed: they are still authorised, still unexecuted,
--           and the next run retries them within the attempt budget.
--
-- 'partial' some executed and some did not. Reported honestly rather than as
--           success, because a caller reading only the status has to be able
--           to trust it.
--
-- 'success' everything authorised executed - or nothing was authorised, which
--           is the normal state of a week in which nobody needed to act.
--
-- records_received  = authorised actions found waiting
-- records_accepted  = executed
-- records_rejected  = failed this run
-- records_duplicate = claimed by another caller between read and write
-- The four balance by construction: every action found gets exactly one
-- outcome, which satisfies the counts CHECK on ingestion_runs.
UPDATE salesops.ingestion_runs r
SET finished_at       = now(),
    records_received  = ($3::int + $4::int + $5::int),
    records_accepted  = $3::int,
    records_rejected  = $4::int,
    records_duplicate = $5::int,
    status            = CASE
                            WHEN $4::int > 0 AND $3::int = 0 THEN 'failed'
                            WHEN $4::int > 0                 THEN 'partial'
                            ELSE 'success'
                        END,
    error_message     = CASE
                            WHEN $4::int > 0
                            THEN $4::text || ' execution failure(s): ' || $6::text
                        END
WHERE r.batch_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING
    run_id,
    batch_id::text AS batch_id,
    status,
    $2::int        AS eligible,
    $3::int        AS executed,
    $4::int        AS failed,
    $5::int        AS skipped,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.remediation_actions
      WHERE status = 'executed')::int                            AS executed_total,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.remediation_actions
      WHERE status = 'proposed')::int                            AS awaiting_authorization,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.remediation_pending_execution)::int
                                                                 AS still_pending,
    -- Reported on every run rather than assumed. The development provider
    -- records requests and contacts nothing, and this is the column that says
    -- so out loud instead of leaving a reader to infer it.
    COALESCE((SELECT bool_or(external_side_effect)
              FROM salesops.remediation_attempts), FALSE)        AS any_external_side_effect,
    round(extract(epoch FROM (finished_at - started_at))::numeric, 2) AS duration_seconds;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('Open Remediation Run').first().json.batch_id, $('Execute Approved Actions').first().json.eligible || 0, $('Execute Approved Actions').first().json.executed || 0, $('Execute Approved Actions').first().json.failed || 0, $('Execute Approved Actions').first().json.skipped || 0, ($('Execute Approved Actions').first().json.failures || []).map(f => f.remediation_id + ' (' + f.reason + ')').join('; ').slice(0, 500) || 'none' ] }}

nodes.notes: Status derived from the service's own counts, not from having reached this node. Also reports how many actions are still waiting on a human to authorise them.

nodes.name: Fail Remediation Run

parameters.query:
-- The service could not be reached, or refused the request outright. Close the
-- run as 'failed' with the reason.
--
-- This branch exists so the workflow always closes its own ledger entry. The
-- error handler covers unexpected failures, but it is invoked by n8n and does
-- not fire in every execution mode - and a run left at 'running' forever is
-- indistinguishable from one still in flight.
--
-- Nothing about the approvals changes. Every authorised action is still
-- authorised and still unexecuted; nothing was half-done, because an action is
-- claimed before the provider is called and released to 'failed' after.
UPDATE salesops.ingestion_runs r
SET finished_at   = now(),
    status        = 'failed',
    error_message = left(
        'Stage 9 execution could not run: ' || COALESCE($2::text, 'unknown error')
        || '. No remediation was executed; every approval remains authorised and '
        || 'unexecuted, and Stage 6, 7 and 8 records are unchanged.',
        1000)
WHERE r.batch_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING
    run_id,
    batch_id::text AS batch_id,
    status,
    error_message,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.remediation_pending_execution)::int
                   AS actions_left_unexecuted;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('Open Remediation Run').first().json.batch_id, ($json.error && ($json.error.message || $json.error.description)) || $json.message || 'the analytics service did not return a result' ] }}

nodes.notes: Closes the run as 'failed' when the service call itself fails. Approvals, decisions, hypotheses and notifications are all untouched.

nodes.name: Close - Nothing Authorized

parameters.query:
-- Nobody authorised anything. Close the run as 'success' and call the service
-- not at all.
--
-- This is a SUCCESS, not a no-op to be embarrassed about. A week in which no
-- anomaly needed a human to authorise a response is a good week, and a stage
-- that reported it as a failure would train people to ignore it.
--
-- The count of actions awaiting authorisation is recorded so that "nothing
-- ran" can be told apart from "nothing ran and four proposals are sitting
-- there waiting for somebody".
UPDATE salesops.ingestion_runs r
SET finished_at       = now(),
    status            = 'success',
    records_received  = 0,
    records_accepted  = 0,
    records_rejected  = 0,
    records_duplicate = 0
WHERE r.batch_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING
    run_id,
    batch_id::text AS batch_id,
    status,
    $2::int        AS awaiting_authorization,
    'No remediation was authorised for execution. Nothing was run.'::text AS note;

nodes.notes: Closes the run as 'success' without calling the service. No authorised work is the normal state, not a fault.
